tess (customer-success): @maria escalating — customer ACME reports streaming JSON responses get cut off mid-object when using our /v1/chat/stream endpoint. They see final chunk end abruptly with no closing brace. Repro curl included.

maria (support): ack. Can you paste the request_id and the exact curl you used? Is this hosted API or Dedicated for ACME?

maria (support): also: any client-side proxy between ACME and our API?


tess (customer-success): request_id: r-0a1b2c3d4e. Hosted API. ACME is behind a corporate edge proxy. Here is the curl they used:

```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-1.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"stream":true}' \
  --max-time 60 > out.sse
```

They attach the end of the payload we got back (truncated):

```
data: {"id":"resp-...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello, here's an ex"},"index":0,"finish_reason":null}]
```

(notice missing closing braces/finish token).

maria (support): thanks. Is there any recent deploy around that time?

deploy-bot: prod-web deploy 2026-03-16T11:05:00Z — deploy/commit abc123 by dan — status: success

dan (eng-runtime): I pulled the request_id logs. Our serving runtime shows the backend finished streaming, wrote trailing bytes, then saw a FIN from the client/proxy immediately after last data chunk:

```
[2026-03-16T11:05:12.345Z] request=r-0a1b2c3d4e state=streaming wrote=4096 tail=0 peer=FIN
```

That matches the truncated tail. Trying to reproduce locally with a corporate proxy emulation (forcing Connection: close) I can reproduce the same cut.

kev (eng-infra): @dan good catch. This smells like an edge timeout/idle-window where a proxy collapses connections after seeing no activity for X secs while our runtime is still finishing multi-chunk JSON events. Do we have the CF/edge request id from the customer?


tess (customer-success): they provided header cf-ray: 7a1c2d3e4f5g6h7i. ACME says they see the socket close ~120ms after last chunk. Their proxy is corporate-gateway v2.1. Repro steps they followed (shortened):

1) curl with -N to keep streaming
2) let the stream run until model finishes (~3.2s)
3) stream file contains truncated JSON as above

They also noted this only happens when their proxy enforces HTTP/1.0 or strips `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`.

dan (eng-runtime): reproduction note: if the proxy downgrades to HTTP/1.0 or removes chunked TE header we end up sending SSE chunks that the proxy aggregates and then emits a single FIN before the final CRLF is flushed. Workaround: ask customer to force TCP keepalive or upgrade proxy config to preserve chunked streaming. As a temporary fix we can offer them to disable streaming and return final JSON (non-stream) so they won't get partial object.

kev (eng-infra): can we add a small server-side guard to send an explicit final zero-length SSE chunk or a short keepalive after final object to ensure proxies have time to flush? Would be low risk.

dan (eng-runtime): technically we could add a final boundary event like `data: [END]\n\n` but that changes SSE semantics. Better short-term: add extra 200ms flush + final CRLF to help flaky proxies. I'll open a PR to runtime with a feature flag.

maria (support): next steps for support: 1) propose workaround to ACME: either disable streaming (non-stream API) or update proxy to preserve chunked TE. 2) ask ACME for a pcap of the request (tcpdump) including the FIN to correlate. 3) eng to triage runtime PR and infra to review edge config.

maria (support): @tess can you send the workaround and request the pcap, then I will open a ticket and assign to eng-runtime + eng-infra?


tess (customer-success): will do. customer asked for ETA — can we get a rough estimate on PR + rollout if we enable the 200ms flush by flag?

 dan (eng-runtime): rough: PR + review ~1d, canary + monitor ~1d, full rollout 2-3d after approvals. I'll link the PR when opened.

maria (support): thanks everyone. tagging internal ticket: SUP-7421. I'll update ACME with the two workarounds and ask for the pcap & cf-ray header. :thumbsup:

tess (customer-success): acked, closing loop once customer responds.
